question: In a phone game played by thousands, what best predicted how happy players felt from moment to moment?
answer: Results compared with expectations, plus the expectations themselves. Rutledge and colleagues fitted a model to more than 18,000 players of a gambling app. Happiness rose when outcomes beat what players expected, but also when they looked forward to a good gamble. Low expectations make good news sweeter while stealing the pleasure of anticipation.
move: Happiness tracks surprises and hopes, not just how things turn out.
ask: Am I keeping my hopes low to avoid disappointment, and losing the pleasure of looking forward?
reference: Rutledge, Skandali, Dayan & Dolan, A computational and neural model of momentary subjective well-being, PNAS, 2014
